weather_stated: late-January 2022 freeze; intensity not seen in Florida for ~20 years
quote: We are anticipating our decline to be approximately 12%-15% year-over-year. We believe this substantially lower rate of decline as compared to the USDA forecast is because of our efficient growth management program
notes: Range -12 to -15; midpoint used. Winter freeze (January), not an Apr-May spring frost. Decline also reflects greening-related fruit drop; freeze share not split out.

quote: USDA is forecasting a 33.9% decline in the current year Valencia crop as compared to the same period in the prior year, with a significant portion of it due to the freeze event.
notes: Industry (USDA) figure; Alico did better than the state thanks to freeze-protection measures. Only part of the decline is freeze.

quote: The processed box production for the three months ended June 30, 2022 decreased by 19.9% as compared to the same period in the prior fiscal year, mainly due to greater fruit drop, which is attributable to disease and weather conditions, including the freeze event
notes: Peak-quarter volume hit; includes disease. Pound solids per box also fell 4% in the quarter.

quote: we are revising our guidance for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2022 to reflect this past season's lower than anticipated internal quality of the Valencia fruit, primarily resulting from the freeze event.
notes: Guidance cut from $35.6-38.9M to $30.7-33.3M (midpoints 37.25 -> 32.0). Part of the cut is ranch-land sales slipping to FY2023, so the freeze share is smaller than -14%. Net income is dominated by land-sale gains, so not a clean profit margin.

weather_stated: January 2022 freeze (plus Hurricane Ian at year end)
quote: Citrus revenue was $89.7 million and $105.8 million for the fiscal years ended September 30th, 2022 and 2021 respectively.
notes: Best single frost-year revenue datapoint. Includes lower grove-management revenue (~-$5M from a terminated contract) and greening; fruit-only effect roughly -10 to -15%. Ian (28 Sep 2022) hit FY2023 crop, not FY2022 revenue.

quote: Our overall box production for fiscal year 2022 was approximately 5.5 million boxes, a decrease of 12.9% as compared to fiscal year 2021.
notes: Early/mid-season crop was mostly picked before the freeze, so the whole-year volume loss is smaller than the Valencia loss.

quote: The USDA in its final citrus crop forecast for the 2021, 2022 harvest season indicated that the Florida orange crop decreased by 22.5% to approximately 41.1 million boxes from approximately 53 million boxes in the prior harvest season.
notes: Industry; freeze is one of several causes (greening is a multi-year drag).

quote: Our average blended price per pound solid increased from $2.45 in the prior fiscal year to $2.63 for the current fiscal year. This was primarily due to tighter supplies of citrus fruit
notes: Price offset: +7.3% price vs -12.9% boxes and lower solids per box; offset recovered roughly a third to a half of the volume loss.

quote: Historically, we've always received for the freeze event and then for Irma, we received the crop insurance within the same year of the event. It's not guaranteed.
notes: Alico's cover is mainly catastrophic (only very large losses pay; see Q4 2022 call). No amount stated for the 2022 freeze.

quote: The unfavorable fixed cost absorption resulted from decreased production levels in New Zealand due to a frost during their harvest season earlier this year, as well as decreased production levels at our wineries in California due to the 2020 U.S. wildfires.
notes: Qualitative. Wine & spirits operating margin fell 620bp in the quarter but for many reasons; frost share not given. Shows frost hits a vertically-integrated wine margin through cost absorption more than through revenue.

weather_stated: late-season (April 2022) frost in Oregon; spotty frost in California
quote: There was for sure issues up there, and the crop is probably gonna be at 50%-60% levels of normal years. It's been a little bit light the last couple of years, so that's not necessarily a surprise.
notes: 50-60% of a normal year = -40 to -50% (midpoint -45). Early estimate in May, versus a normal year not prior year. Company revenue effect not given (wine inventory buffers it).

quote: There has been an impact, which if you take, our domain has been quite limited to 15% still, though, of the total production. In fact, the quality is very good, and the productivity per hectare also has been very good
notes: Own estate ~-15% production; CEO says Cognac less hit than other French regions and impact on the group 'not so material' (aged eaux-de-vie stocks).

impact_metric: volume available for sale (2-3 yrs later)
quote: It has a very limited impact to poor harvest, for whatever reason, being frost or heat or whatever. It's not increasing the unit cost. It diminishes the amount of bottles that is available in the next two to three years after the aging process.
notes: Qualitative. Aged-product makers (and Champagne/Cognac reserve systems) defer and smooth frost losses; not representative of fresh-fruit growers.

weather_stated: April 2021 spring frost plus vine disease
quote: You know that the harvest this year is the lowest since many years in France due to the frost we had in spring in April due to also some diseases in the vines
notes: Qualitative industry statement from a glass-bottle supplier. 2021 France frost is the cleanest example of the Apr-May peril; no grower revenue figure in Quartr.

quote: We lost some 500 tons to frost and ultimately had a bloom that did not quite deliver.
notes: 500 t against a ~29.5-30 kt crop (analyst framing in H2 2024 call: s287064298949737822117) = ~-1.7%. A mild frost year; the rest of the 2025 shortfall was bloom/crack-out, not frost.

weather_stated: late spring frost (Oct 2022) plus hail, cyclones, warm winter
quote: Revenue at NZD 39.9 million, is down 13%, really reflects the impact of lower yields, frost, hail, and lower OGRs from Zespri. EBITDA, negative NZD 1.9 million, as I previously said. SunGold is down at the 22%.
notes: Mixed perils (frost, hail, cyclone) and lower per-tray returns; frost not isolated. Company said lowest Hayward yields in 10 years (s79058022048804985110785).

quote: Well, quite simply, we've been frosted and hailed. The yields are down, and look, you know, we've got to take a prediction of what we think the fruit's gonna sell for.
notes: Orcharding EBITDA NZD 5.1M -> -1.9M (NZD; change NZD -7.0M, USD not stated). Profit fell ~10x more than revenue (-13%). CEO: 'quite sensitive to changes in yields'.

weather_stated: severe freeze in Turkey and weather issues in Spain
quote: Turkey had a really challenging freeze, which, it's always hard to get the best assessment, but could have gone all the way down to damaging trees, which would be two years of crop. Also, Spain had their own set of weather issues. Next year we see Spain and Turkey being short, call it 20% to 30%
notes: Opposite side of the trade: a frost elsewhere lifted Limoneira's August lemon prices to low $20s from ~$17 per carton. Tree damage can make a freeze a two-year loss.

weather_stated: below-freezing conditions last week of January 2022
quote: At this time, given these uncertainties and the lower anticipated box production and the average pound-size per box expected this season before the recent freeze, we are withdrawing our previously issued guidance
notes: Context row: guidance withdrawn right after the freeze; later cut ~14% (see Q3 2022 row).

weather_stated: most severe drought in at least half a century in the U.S.
quote: Although this was the largest crop planted since 1973, production is now forecast to be 13% below last year, and the yield of 123.4 bushels per acre is down almost 24 bushels per acre from last year.
notes: USDA Aug-2012 numbers quoted by Deere's chief economist. Yield -24 bu on ~147 = about -16% (yield loss); production fell less because more acres were planted. Final 2012 numbers were worse than this August estimate.

quote: For soybeans, production is forecast down 12% from last year.
notes: Yield cut to 36.1 bu/acre.

quote: Cash receipts last year, 2011, were an all-time record. Despite the reduced output due to drought, receipts are expected to be even larger for 2012.
notes: Key price-offset evidence: in a breadbasket drought the price rise plus insurance more than offset the volume loss in aggregate. Does not hold for an individual farm whose loss is worse than average, or for a local drought.

impact_metric: crop insurance indemnities (share of gross cash income)
quote: Total crop insurance payments for 2012 are expected to be in the $15 billion-$16 billion range. As of last week, crop insurance industry payouts totaled roughly $13.5 billion. At the high range, this equates to about 4% of 2012 forecast gross cash income.
notes: Insurance offset ~4% of sector gross income (vs ~$10.8B in 2011). About 85% of corn/soy acres were insured (s50259125160503247351553); revenue-protection policies reset to harvest price.

quote: Again, assuming trend yields in normal weather conditions, corn yields are forecast to increase about 31%, while soybean yields are forecast to be up about 12%.
notes: Implied 2012 shortfall vs trend: corn 1-1/1.31 = -24%, soybeans 1-1/1.12 = -11%. Closest thing to a 'management weather estimate' of the drought yield effect.

quote: While the farm sector remains strong, above normal temperatures have lowered the yield projections in the CIS by about 20%.
notes: Heat-led drought; vs earlier projections.

weather_stated: worst drought of the last 100 years (La Nina)
quote: However, we expect yields for our 22/23 crops campaign to be between 30%-40% lower compared to historical levels.
notes: Range -30 to -40 vs historical (CEO said vs previous year in same call). No rainfall % given.

weather_stated: worst drought of the last 100 years
quote: Now, starting from the most affected segment, our crop business simply broke even compared to the $18 million generated last year.
notes: Crop adj. EBITDA $18M -> $0.196M. Also hit by higher USD costs and 6% less planted area. Profit fell ~3x more than yields (operating leverage on fixed per-hectare costs).

quote: In the rice business, we completed harvesting activities with only 6% reduction in yields, but better prices and logistics, so we had better margins.
notes: Irrigated crop in the same drought lost only 6% and margins rose. Irrigated farms should get a much lower drought elasticity.

quote: On the other hand, total production in our farming division reported a 27% year-over-year reduction, mostly explained by crops, due to the effects of an unprecedented drought in Argentina, which impacted area and volume produced.
notes: Includes rice/dairy (less hit) and lower planted area; crops alone fell more.

quote: The Argentinian government passed a resolution that allowed for the use of a preferential FX rate to convert the proceeds from sales of rice, soybean, corn, peanut, and sunflower, which partially offset the decrease in yields.
notes: Offset came from a policy FX rate, not world prices (Argentina's drought did not move world prices much). Crop H1 EBITDA only $0.5M.

weather_stated: most severe drought of the country in more than 100 years
impact_metric: crop volume (Argentina soybeans vs initial forecast)
quote: The country lost 50% of the soybeans and 35% of the corn that was budget, that was forecast at the beginning of the planted plantation area time.
notes: National: soybeans -50%, corn -35%, wheat -40% vs initial forecasts.

quote: Cresud was 30%-40% of the wheat, 18%-35% of the corn, 30%-50% of the soybeans, meaning diversification on regions works.
notes: Own losses vs budget: soybeans -30 to -50 (midpoint -40), corn -18 to -35, wheat -30 to -40. Geographic spread cut losses vs national.

weather_stated: drought plus early frost on 18 Feb 2023
quote: This is a combination of the drought, plus a early frozen that we suffered in the 18th of February that made us majority of our soybean, second soybean and the first soybean to suffer. The 30% drop is because of the combination of the drought plus the early frozen.
notes: Corn yields only -3% YoY; regional tonnage -4% YoY across all countries.

quote: Cresud kept majority of the soybean and the corn and was finally finishing selling much better prices, so compensating majority of the drought effect.
notes: Management claims prices (incl. government FX compensation) offset most of the loss; CFO notes operating results still fell (lower yields, higher costs).

weather_stated: lack of rainfall in the north
quote: Talking about this, we can share that in Paraguay, the reduction was dramatic. We can see 90% or close to a 100% drop on yield.
notes: Local near-total failure; shows max loss per farm can approach 100% of crop. Range -90 to -100.

weather_stated: water deficit Apr-May 2022 (rains failed in May) plus frost
quote: We had 20% of losses between cotton and corn. We expect a normal year, and as such, we will continue to operate at good levels.
notes: Revenue still hit a record (+33.8% Q2) on high prices and a big soybean crop; margins stayed in 31-39% guidance. Lower yields also saved variable costs (cost/ha +14.1% vs +16.1% budget).

impact_metric: crop volume (South America soybeans vs initial estimates)
quote: soybean production in South America had losses of approximately 31 million tons, that is 20%, as compared to the initial estimates for the region.
notes: Industry-level.

weather_stated: El Nino; significant reduction in rainfall Oct-Dec 2023
quote: We reached 3,276 kilos per hectare, 17% lower than budget and 1% higher than the national average.
notes: Growing-season dry spell (southern-hemisphere spring). Soybean prices were also lower, so no price offset this time.

quote: Net income of almost R$229 million was unfortunately 60% lower than Q1 2023 and adjusted EBITDA reached R$700 million, with an adjusted EBITDA margin of 36%.
notes: Profit fell ~3.5x the soybean yield shortfall; also lower prices. Revenue ~R$2.0B.

quote: Soybean, estimated between estimated and actual, 218,000 tons. Actual, 204,000 tons, with a variance of 6%, 6% less.
notes: One large farm in drought pulled the company total 6% below plan.

weather_stated: drought during June and partly May 2023
quote: Our Farming companies, the group Farming companies, harvested 4% less crop than last year, mainly due to summer crop yields. We had that drought during June, partly May, which actually impacted the possible yields, but we were expecting that it might make more damage.
notes: A mild May-June dry spell; matches Hone's May-Aug window.

weather_stated: persistent widespread drought in almost all of Europe (summer 2022)
quote: resulting in an expected sugar production from beet of 3.8 million tons, against 3.2 million tons in the previous year.
notes: Computed vs the following normal-ish year: 3.2/3.8 = -16%; campaign days 107 vs ~120 (-11%). Südzucker is a processor, but beet yield loss is the growers' loss.

quote: The increase was achieved despite declining sales volumes due to the poor 2022 harvest, thanks to significantly higher prices.
notes: Price offset exceeded the volume loss for the processor (EU tight market + inflation).

quote: Participation rents decreased primarily due to lower yields, coupled with lower pricing for last year's crops. The lower yields were expected due to the fact that these crops were harvested at the end of a multi-year drought
notes: $7.7M -> $5.9M. Mixed with lower almond prices (oversupply). Irrigated permanent crops: drought works through water allocations, not May-Aug rain.

quote: The negative impact of the drought is really having a 2023 impact equal to or greater than the drought impact in during the 2022 financial year.
notes: Qualitative. Nut/fruit marketing tails push drought revenue loss into the next year. Row-crop farmland (Midwest) did well in 2022.
